To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temporal correlations of a network of randomly coupled rotators are described by a differential equation for the self-consistency of the autocorrelation function.

(i) the autocorrelation function of randomly coupled rotators can be described by a differential equation that is self-consistent, i.e., it contains the autocorrelation as a functional argument, (ii) this differential equation can be solved analyti-cally for special cases, (iii) the numerical solutions of the differential equation are confirmed by simulations of randomly coupled rotors, and (iv) the theory is generalized to pulse-coupled rotators and confirmed by simulations of a standard model
the self-consistent correlation function can be calculated from a differential equation that can be solved for a large variety of scenarios.
